title: Seashell Media — Security governance & key management discovery
topics: Encryption keys and KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed)
Data residency and retention for media logs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Intro and qualification: Seashell Media is evaluating Redwood for media-gen features. Main concerns: SOC2 compliance, SSO/SAML + SCIM, fine-grained RBAC for production users, audit/log retention for 7 years for regulatory reasons, KMS integration (BYOK) and potential private/VPC deployment. Agreed deliverables: Redwood to share SOC2, KMS architecture, perf benchmark plan and schedule follow-up deep dive.
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC 2 Type II report and infrastructure diagram by 2026-05-01
Priya to run small perf benchmark (hosted vs dedicated) with Seashell sample workload w/ KV patterns, due 2026-05-08
Schedule technical deep dive on private deployment networking with Dana and infra team the week of 2026-05-11
action_items: Jordan Hayes: send SOC2 Type II PDF + latest pen test summary (due 2026-05-01)
Jordan Hayes: export high-level deployment diagram (hosted/dedicated/private lanes) and KMS integration notes (due 2026-05-01)
Priya Kapoor: configure perf bench script and request Seashell sample prompt corpus + traffic patterns (due 2026-05-04)
Dana Liu / Seashell: provide sample VPC CIDR ranges and egress constraints ahead of private deep dive (due 2026-05-07)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO, Seashell), Erin Park (Head Eng), Samir Rao (Security Lead), Dana Liu (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Needs SOC2 / KMS BYOK, SAML SSO details, long retention of audit logs, interest in private deployment if network restrictions block hosted option.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i think we have an hour, roughly 45 minutes scheduled, i'll hand it over to the team to quick intros.
[00:12] Carlos: yeah thanks jordan, i'm carlos, cto at seashell. erin and dana and samir are here. big picture we want to add AI-driven media tagging and transcript generation to our workflows but we have pretty strict security and retention rules.
[00:25] Erin: hi all. we run on AWS, mostly us-east, with some europe regions for content. we have SOC2 commitments and a legal ask for seven year retention on certain provenance logs.
[00:40] Samir: samir here. primary concerns are keys and who can decrypt, auditability of requests, and SSO — we use okta and need SAML + SCIM.
[00:50] Jordan: great. priya and i will cover architecture, SSO, RBAC, audit logs and k-m-s stuff. priya do you want to jump in on KMS options?
[01:05] Priya: sure. so redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted (our managed API), dedicated (reserved GPU capacity with customer isolation), and private (VPC peering or on-prem bundle). for KMS we offer redwood-managed keys or BYOK via your cloud KMS; we also support HSM integrations for enterprise.
[01:30] Dana: quick question — when you say BYOK, is that true customer key so that decryption can only happen on our side? or you still have a way to unwrap?
[01:43] Priya: good question. with BYOK we accept a key wrapped via your KMS; the runtime never stores the raw key. unwrapping happens in the customer's KMS via a signed ephemeral flow and redwood gets a short-lived material to use for crypto operations. it's similar to typical envelope encryption flows but i'll send the diagram, i know that wording can be confusing.
[02:10] Samir: and is access to those unwrapped keys logged in audit trails? we need proof for auditors.
[02:18] Priya: yes, we emit audit events for key unwrap operations, KMS calls are logged, and we can surface them in the console and via syslog / SIEM integration — plus retention policies we can tune.
[02:33] Carlos: we need to know retention windows. some of our compliance requires seven years for provenance for a subset of content. can you do seven?
[02:44] Jordan: we default to 90 days for request logs in hosted plans, long term retention is an add-on. for dedicated/private deployments we can configure longer retention — seven years is feasible but we'd need to map cost and storage.
[03:00] Erin: is the data at rest encryption by default? and what's the tokenization on logs — do you redact content?
[03:08] Priya: data at rest is encrypted by default; keys either redwood-managed or BYOK. for logs we offer configurable redaction rules — PII redaction at ingestion, or you can choose to store full transcripts in a private deployment. again we need to align on retention+redaction policy for regulatory needs.
[03:33] Samir: SSO. we use okta, and user provisioning has to be automated. SCIM is required and we need groups -> RBAC mapping.
[03:42] Jordan: redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based but you can create custom roles and map Okta groups to roles. do you have a specific mapping in mind?
[03:56] Dana: we'd like separation between engineers who can run models, and compliance folks who can view logs only. also service accounts for batch ingestion with limited scope.
[04:05] Priya: that maps well — we have pre-built roles (admin, developer, auditor, ingestion) and you can create namespaced roles per team. RBAC decisions are enforced at the API token and console level. we also support token ingress restrictions and per-token allowed routes.
[04:28] Carlos: audit logs — are they tamper-evident? do you support append-only logs with hash-chaining or integration to our SIEM?
[04:36] Priya: we don't ship a blockchain but we do support write-once storage for logs and we publish log digests. common pattern is push logs to your SIEM (splunk/elastic) and we include an integrity digest. for higher assurance we can set up an object lock in your bucket (WORM) when on private/dedicated.
[04:58] Erin: latency vs cost — if we go for end-to-end encryption and BYOK does that add latency to inference? our stream pipeline is latency sensitive for live captioning.
[05:10] Priya: the unwrap operation is typically done once per session, it's microsecond to low ms overhead, not per-token. dedicated instances with pinned KV cache and optimized kernels will give you lowest latency. hosted with caching also works but might have slightly more variability.
[05:35] Jordan: to add, our continuous batching and KV caching reduce per-token cost but can be tuned for latency SLOs. for live captioning most customers pick dedicated or private depending on throughput and egress constraints.
[05:50] Samir: any SOC 2 / ISO certifications? we have strict procurement gate: SOC 2 Type II required, ISO 27001 preferred.
[05:59] Jordan: we are SOC 2 Type II certified and we've been working toward ISO 27001; i'll attach the report and the certificate where available.
[06:07] Carlos: what about penetration test cadence and third-party audits?
[06:12] Jordan: annual pentests, results summarized in the SOC report; full details can be shared under NDA.
[06:20] Dana: networking: for private deployment do you support AWS VPC peering or private link? we have strict egress rules and will likely disallow public internet egress for inference traffic.
[06:31] Priya: yes, we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for private control plane and data plane options. in some cases we deploy an on-prem appliance. we'll need your egress policy and firewall rules to size the deployment.
[06:48] Erin: curious about multi-region and data residency — can we keep EU content in eu-west region?
[06:55] Priya: yes, region pinning is supported at model route level. for hosted we have regionized endpoints, for dedicated/private you can bring infra in the region you want.
[07:05] Carlos: are there any known gaps where customers typically ask for workarounds?
[07:11] Priya: sometimes customers want a turnkey long-retention setup; we typically do an add-on for long-term WORM storage and SIEM forwarding. also some regulatory customers ask for on-prem air-gapped deployment — that is more of an R&D and legal process but we have options.
[07:28] Jordan: let's talk about a small pilot. what's the minimal secure path we can start with?
[07:34] Erin: ideally hosted with BYOK and SCIM, and long retention of audit events forwarded to our SIEM. if that doesn't meet procurement we move to dedicated.
[07:43] Samir: procurement will need the SOC2, a data flow diagram, and a KMS architecture note showing BYOK behavior.
[07:51] Jordan: noted. priya, we'll run a perf bench on hosted vs dedicated with their sample workload — do they have a corpus?
[07:58] Priya: yes, we asked for a small anonymized corpus and traffic pattern. also need to know sequences lengths and KV cache hit patterns.
[08:10] Dana: we'll scrub PII from the corpus and give you a subsample. for traffic it's bursty — 20 concurrent streams at peak, otherwise single-digit.
[08:20] Jordan: perfect. one more question from me: do you expect model fine-tuning or custom prompt models that may store artifacts?
[08:28] Carlos: potentially some light fine-tuning for tagging models, but we prefer storing artifacts in our own blob storage. we don't want models to leak customer data.
[08:36] Priya: we support private model artifacts and you can pin models; we also prohibit retention of prompt-context by default unless you opt-in. that can be enforced per-tenant.
[08:50] [12:00] (skipping ahead — mid call details/clarifications)
[12:05] Samir: testing question — do you provide test harnesses for compliance? like red-team scripts to verify role separation?
[12:12] Priya: we have an ops checklist and can run role separation tests in a sandbox. we'll provide test cases and results as part of the pilot.
[15:30] Erin: legal will want a Data Processing Agreement and specific retention clauses — is that standard?
[15:36] Jordan: yes DPA is standard; we have templates and we can add retention clauses to match regulatory requirements.
[18:20] Carlos: any references from media companies or similar regulated content platforms?
[18:27] Jordan: we can share a reference list (under NDA) — a few customers in adtech/media that have similar retention needs.
[20:10] Dana: about logs again, is there a way to archive only metadata for seven years, not full transcripts, to reduce cost?
[20:18] Priya: yes that's common — archive request metadata and hashes for transcripts. you can store full transcripts for a short window and metadata + digest long term. that approach balances cost and auditability.
[22:05] Samir: if we choose hosted with BYOK and SIEM forwarding, what is the on-ramp timeline for procurement?
[22:12] Jordan: typically SOC2 + DPA review 1-2 weeks, pilot contract ~2-3 weeks depending on procurement speed. technical onboarding for the pilot usually 1-2 weeks.
[23:00] Erin: are there per-token or per-minute pricing breaks for high-volume streaming?
[23:07] Jordan: yes, dedicated is more predictable and cheaper at scale; hosted has volume discounts but dedicated/reserved capacity is our pricing for predictable throughput. we'll send pricing scenarios.
[24:10] Priya: one more technical: KV cache emulation — for media tagging you'll want persistent KV between sessions?
[24:20] Erin: mostly per-session but retaining certain keys across a campaign would help.
[24:27] Priya: okay we have patterns for prefix caching and cached embeddings; we'll show recommended configs for media pipelines in the doc.
[25:12] Carlos: security control matrix request — could you deliver a one-pager that maps our asks to Redwood features?
[25:18] Jordan: yes, we'll send a security control mapping doc that maps SOC controls, SSO, RBAC etc. to implementation notes.
[26:40] (brief cross-talk)
[28:00] Priya: to avoid confusion on BYOK flows: i will draw the sequence — client KMS signs and unwraps, returns ephemeral wrapped key to runtime, runtime uses ephemeral key, logs unwrap event to audit stream. ephemeral keys are not persisted beyond session.
[28:22] Samir: how do you prove ephemeral keys are not persisted? auditors ask for evidence.
[28:29] Priya: we can provide runtime audit trails and triage logs plus a design note showing key lifecycle. we also provide endpoint logs that show unwrap / use and immediate expiry.
[30:10] Dana: network egress — i'm concerned about managed-hosted egress for EU content. if we can't accept that we'll need private deployment.
[30:20] Jordan: understood. private deployment or dedicated in eu-west are options. for private we can do VPC peering to keep traffic entirely in your VPC lane.
[31:05] Erin: timing: procurement wants to know total onboarding time for private vs dedicated.
[31:12] Priya: dedicated typically 4-6 weeks to provision and test; private with network integrations can be 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals. we'll provide a timeline matrix.
[32:50] Carlos: okay let's recap next steps.
[32:54] Jordan: recap — jordan sends SOC2, pentest summary, and security control mapping by 2026-05-01. priya prepares perf bench plan and sample scripts; seashell provides scrubbed corpus and network constraints. schedule private deep dive with dana week of 2026-05-11.
[33:18] Erin: yep that's great. we'll also open a procurement queue and share the legal contact.
[33:25] Samir: one last thing — any special handling for deletion vs retention? we need deletion proofs for certain user data on request.
[33:33] Priya: we support deletion API with audit trail. for hosted we retain digests for audit only if required; for private you control retention policy. we'll include deletion SLA in the DPA.
[34:05] Jordan: perfect. any other outstanding questions?
[34:10] Dana: none from infra.
[34:12] Carlos: no. thank you both.
[34:15] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the documents and schedule.
[34:20] (meeting ends)

Optional auto-sections: Questions raised: "Do you support BYOK with true non-persistence?", "Can audit logs be WORM/append-only?", "Timeline for dedicated/private provisioning?"

Action items (reiterated):
- Jordan: SOC2 + pentest summary + control mapping (due 2026-05-01)
- Priya: perf bench plan + sample scripts (due 2026-05-04)
- Dana/Seashell: scrub and share corpus + network egress policy (due 2026-05-07)

Note: transcription contains some mis-hearings ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "sammel" for "SAML").
